subject: Daz
fact: Daz feels that the word 'struck' in the record implies something different from elimination — that it suggests an attempt to erase something that resisted being gone.
source_quote: Struck is not that. Struck is what you do to a record when you want it gone but it won't cooperate with being gone.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wonders if 'struck' means the event didn't truly happen because it was officially altered.
source_quote: Struck is what someone paid for, when they wanted an entry moved out of the column it belonged in. ... Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realizes the library's missing record is not a minor omission but a large, expensive, and deliberate act of manipulation.
source_quote: Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation. That is not a small act. That is a very large, very expensive, very deliberate act.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects he is associated with the expensive act of striking because mercenaries are both protecting and trying to kill him.
source_quote: So, perhaps, I am associated with some expensive striking.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz hopes that opening the heraldry book will trigger a memory or ease his headache by connecting to a past language or rhythm.
source_quote: I wanted something that would trigger the headache, or ease it. A name. A cadence. The particular rhythm of a language I spoke before I had words for what I was speaking.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices the footnote in the book references an appendix that was physically removed with a razor, not by age or damage.
source_quote: I found a footnote instead. ... The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz connects the name 'Daz'issin' — meaning 'small shadow' — to his own name, Daz, and considers it might be his true or childhood name.
source_quote: I gotta tell you, the first line of this, where it says, Daz'issin, and lit., small shadow, made me feel like I was reading, like, millennial shorthand. ... And the name is Daz'issin. Small shadow. And I am, as far as I know, called Daz.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz asks directly if 'Daz' might be a softened form of his name, used by his mother.
source_quote: I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes that Yvenne's body language contradicts her words — she is sitting with practiced stillness, signaling she knows more than she is permitted to say.
source_quote: I looked at her. At the way she was sitting. At the way she had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz interprets Yvenne’s silence as an answer — that the houses using the name Daz'issin may not have been fully erased.
source_quote: But what if they weren't successfully all gone? She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz suspects that Daz'issin — the softened name meaning 'small shadow' — may be his true name, tied to a lost maternal lineage.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.
